sections.title: Strong emotions
sections.content:
Advanced vocabulary allows us to express emotions with greater precision:
• elated — extremely happy. She was elated when she received the scholarship.
• devastated — extremely shocked and upset. He was devastated by the sudden loss.
• bewildered — completely confused. The complex instructions left everyone bewildered.
• exasperated — intensely irritated. The teacher became exasperated with the constant interruptions.
• apprehensive — anxious about the future. Many students feel apprehensive before exams.

sections.title: Subtle feelings
sections.content:
Some feelings are less intense but equally important to express:
• nostalgic — longing for the past. The old photographs made her feel nostalgic.
• ambivalent — having mixed feelings. He felt ambivalent about the job offer — excited but nervous.
• indifferent — having no particular interest. She seemed completely indifferent to the criticism.
• contemplative — deeply thoughtful. He sat in a contemplative mood, staring at the rain.
• wistful — feeling sad longing. She gave a wistful smile remembering her childhood.

sections.title: Reactions to situations
sections.content:
How people react can be described with specific vocabulary:
• taken aback — surprised and slightly shocked. I was taken aback by his rude comment.
• overwhelmed — feeling too much at once. She felt overwhelmed by all the responsibility.
• reassured — feeling less worried. His calm voice reassured me that everything would be fine.
• disheartened — losing hope or confidence. Don't be disheartened by one failure.

exercises.question: If you feel extremely happy about an achievement, you are:
exercises.hint: It's an extreme form of happiness.
exercises.explanation: Elated means ecstatically happy, often after achieving something.

exercises.question: Someone who has mixed feelings about something is:
exercises.hint: They can't decide if they feel positive or negative.
exercises.explanation: Ambivalent means having conflicting feelings about something.

exercises.question: Which phrase means 'surprised and slightly shocked'?
exercises.explanation: Taken aback means surprised, often in a negative way.

exercises.question: Feeling anxious or worried about something in the future is:
exercises.hint: It relates to uncertainty about what's coming.
exercises.explanation: Apprehensive means feeling worried about something that might happen.

exercises.question: A person who shows no interest or concern is:
exercises.explanation: Indifferent means having no particular interest or sympathy.

exercises.question: Feeling a gentle sadness when remembering the past is being:
exercises.explanation: Wistful means having a feeling of vague or regretful longing.

exercises.question: If too many tasks make you feel you can't cope, you are:
exercises.explanation: Overwhelmed means feeling unable to deal with the volume of something.

exercises.question: Which word means 'losing hope or confidence'?
exercises.explanation: Disheartened means having lost determination or confidence.
